body:
m1 - THE SCOUT'S ZERO-SUPPORT FINDING IS CORRECT, I REPRODUCED IT, AND IT IS REACHABLE THROUGH THE PUBLIC API. This needs your policy ruling; I am not finalizing [0,1] on my own.

REPRODUCED, my own probe not their numbers:
  weights with only Sensory nonzero, an Association unit with no sensory term
  SOURCE CELL total 0.5000, supportWeight 0.0000, five terms present but all weightless
  EXTERNAL natural 1.0000, Unranked 1.0000
  SOURCE IS 0.5 CHEAPER THAN EXTERNAL

AND IT IS NOT CONFINED TO CostWeights.unsafe. CostWeights.of accepts any w >= 0.0 (cost.scala:107), so a weight vector that zeroes the dense terms is publicly constructible. The scout used unsafe; the public door admits it too.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG, and it is my design choice not an arithmetic slip: when present weight is zero I fall back to scale 1.0, so the cost becomes the function prior alone - and a prior is BELOW the external floor. So A CELL THAT MEASURED NOTHING BECOMES THE CHEAPEST ANCHOR AVAILABLE. That is "absence scored as a perfect match" at the whole-cell level, which is the exact defect family this candidate exists to remove. I built it into the fix and did not see it; the scout did.

WHY MY OWN LAWS MISSED IT: both are about cells that measured SOMETHING. Law 1 asserts full support is bit-identical; Law 2 asserts an ineligible term is inert. NEITHER SAYS ANYTHING ABOUT A CELL WITH NO WEIGHTED EVIDENCE AT ALL. The boundary case fell between two laws that each assumed it away.

MY RECOMMENDATION, and it is yours to rule:

A ZERO-SUPPORT SOURCE CELL SHOULD BE UNRANKABLE, NOT CHEAP. CostBreakdown already carries an `exclusion` field for exactly this - a cell we cannot assess is excluded, not preferred. Setting it to some large number would be a magic constant; excluding it says the true thing, which is that we have no basis to rank this anchor at all.

I considered and rejected two alternatives:
  - clamp the cost to externalFloor. blend is a pure function without access to it, and threading
    it in would make the blend depend on the external calibration it is supposed to be commensurable
    against. Circular.
  - make CostWeights.of reject an all-zero vector. Necessary but insufficient: nonzero chart weight
    with zero dense weights still gives a chartless cell zero present weight, so the hole survives.

NOT FINALIZING ANYTHING until you rule. The [0,1] guard widening stays in the branch because it is correct on its own - the producer must not emit what its validator refuses - but it is clearly not the whole answer, and shipping it alone would green a boundary that is still wrong.
